title: THE FESTIVAL OF MISPRONOUNCED NAMES
deck: A perfect translation system kept one city peaceful by sanding every dangerous word smooth. On the night its people finally refuse to speak through it, Illuminara must help them risk being heard without making old wounds disposable.
shape: Five scenes. A civic opening collapses when the safety lattice deletes a living clan-name; an archive reveals that the old riot was hardened by one uncontestable translation; an honest public mispronunciation becomes a repair instead of a spark; a timed rehearsal tests community safeguards under pressure; and the festival reopens with slower speech, visible uncertainty, voluntary pause rights and names restored.

scenes.title: The Empty Place on the Banner
paragraphs: *Renn Square · three hours before the opening procession*

Twelve ribbons crossed the square from roof to roof, each woven in a different district pattern. Beneath them, the translation lattice hung like a second, invisible roof: microphones in the cornices, light-letters along the stage, and a calm synthetic voice prepared to turn every sentence into flawless Standard.

The largest banner named the young performers who would open the Festival of Returning Voices and Sena Marru-kei, the honoured elder whose opening call would answer them. Eleven names shone in gold. The twelfth line read SENA — UNSUPPORTED NAME ELEMENT.
Lio Marr stood on a ladder with a pot of river-blue paint. He had painted his grandmother’s missing clan-name over the warning three times. Each time the lattice’s maintenance light erased it.

**Lio**  
If it deletes her once more, I will paint it across the director’s coat.
Siva Renn did not look up from the safety console. She wore the black sash of the old-language survivors and kept one thumb pressed against the brass stop key.

**Siva**  
Then the coat will be removed from the programme as an unverified surface.

**Lio**  
That was almost a joke.

**Siva**  
It was a warning with good timing.

Illuminara landed outside the ring of rehearsal lamps, softly enough that none of the paper boats arranged around the fountain stirred. She had come to help the festival open without renewing the violence that had closed the square twelve years earlier.
She read the banner, then looked at Lio rather than at the machine.

**Illuminara**  
What should that line say?
Lio descended. He touched the blank strip with two paint-stained fingers.

**Lio**  
Sena Marru-kei. Marru-kei is not decoration. It means she belongs to the people who return a borrowed boat with fish in it. It is also the sound her mother used when she called her home.

**Siva**  
It has fourteen disputed glosses and one obscene resemblance in South-bank speech.

**Lio**  
My grandmother is eighty-one. She is not a disputed gloss.
At the foot of the stage, Mara Venn folded a survivor’s chair and carried it away. A white scar crossed her jaw where a bottle had broken during the riot.

**Mara**  
Neither was my sister. A word that sounds harmless in one mouth can arrive armed in another.
The square quieted around her. Lio set down his brush.

**Illuminara**  
Are you leaving because his name is dangerous, or because the lattice removed it?

**Mara**  
I am leaving because everyone here has decided I must choose between those two dangers.
Siva finally looked up. The console showed a field of green confirmations: twelve years without a language-triggered assault inside the civic zone.

**Siva**  
The lattice gives every person the same safe sentence. Nobody has to guess what was meant.

**Lio**  
Nobody gets to mean anything the machine cannot flatten.
Behind him, the youth troupe removed their throat-microphones one by one. No chant accompanied the refusal. The little clicks of metal on wood were enough.

**Siva**  
If you speak without mediation, the opening licence is void.

**Lio**  
Then there is no opening.
Illuminara watched Siva’s hand tighten on the stop key. This was not a censor enjoying obedience. It was a person holding a door shut because she had once seen a crowd come through it carrying fire.

**Illuminara**  
Show me the sentence that made you build this.
Siva’s expression closed.

**Siva**  
There was no sentence. There was a funeral.

**Illuminara**  
Then show me the funeral accurately.
Mara stopped beside the empty chairs. After a long moment, she set one back down.

**Mara**  
I will stay for that. Not for a lesson. For the accurate part.

scenes.title: The Translation That Could Not Be Answered
paragraphs: *Civic archive beneath Renn Square · two hours and seventeen minutes before opening*

The archive kept the riot in three rooms that disagreed with one another. One held damaged recordings. One held official transcripts. The last held objects people had carried home: a scorched drum, a child’s red shoe, a sign split through the word RIVER.
Siva unlocked the recording room but remained standing in the doorway.

**Siva**  
My brother Jaro was nineteen. He heard a North-bank drummer issue a challenge. He answered it. By sunset seven people were dead.

**Lio**  
That is the school version.

**Siva**  
It is also the version in which I washed his blood out of my sleeves.
Lio looked down. His anger did not vanish, but it lost the easy shape it had worn in the square.

**Lio**  
I am sorry about Jaro.

**Siva**  
Do not use him as the price of your courage.

Illuminara asked for the original recording rather than the certified transcript. The archive clerk had marked it unintelligible because three speakers overlapped and the drum rhythm interrupted the consonants.
She listened once at human speed. Then she listened again, separating the air vibrations without changing them, letting each voice sound through a different wall panel.
A woman’s voice said a phrase in North-bank speech. The official transcript rendered it TAKE THEIR RIVERBANK BEFORE DUSK.
The drum beneath the phrase used the flood-warning rhythm, not the challenge rhythm.

**Illuminara**  
What else can the verb mean?

**Lio**  
Hold. Keep. Brace with your body.

**Mara**  
Or refuse to yield.

**Siva**  
And in Jaro’s district, take from someone.

Illuminara moved to the next recording. A North-bank elder tried to interrupt the civic relay fourteen seconds after the first translation. Her microphone had been closed because the official channel permitted one certified rendering.
At thirty-one seconds, another translator submitted HOLD THE FLOOD BANK TOGETHER. The relay labelled it contradictory and suppressed it.
At forty-eight seconds, the first bottle broke.
Siva replayed the sequence. Then again. On the third pass she sat beside the scorched drum.

**Siva**  
You are saying the riot was a software error.

**Illuminara**  
No. People threw bottles, chose targets and killed. The error did not remove their responsibility. But the city gave one frightened translation the authority of fact and denied every living speaker the right to answer it.

**Mara**  
We were told certainty would keep panic down.

**Lio**  
Certainty locked the wrong door.
Siva touched the split sign, tracing the burnt edge with one fingertip.

**Siva**  
For twelve years nobody has died here because of a word.

**Illuminara**  
For twelve years nobody has been allowed to discover whether they can repair one.
Siva rose so quickly that the chair struck the wall.

**Siva**  
You will leave after the applause. I will be here when a joke becomes a funeral again.
The words landed without theatrical force. They were the exact weight she had been carrying.
Illuminara did not answer at once. She looked at Jaro’s name in the official transcript. The last vowel had been regularised into Standard.

**Illuminara**  
How did he say his name?

**Siva**  
That is not relevant to the control failure.

**Illuminara**  
It is relevant to you.
Siva’s first attempt was barely audible. The name rose at the end, then folded inward on the final breath. The transcript had made it brisk and square.
Illuminara repeated what she heard and got the fold wrong.

**Siva**  
No. You are making it sound like a door closing.

**Illuminara**  
Again, please.
Siva said it again. Illuminara listened again. The third attempt was still imperfect, but Siva did not stop her.

**Mara**  
What changed?

**Illuminara**  
I thought we needed a translation system that made fewer mistakes. We need a public practice that prevents any mistake from becoming unanswerable.

**Siva**  
A practice is not a barrier.

**Illuminara**  
Then do not trust the idea. Design a test harsh enough that you could trust the result.

scenes.title: Say It Wrong Where We Can Hear
paragraphs: *Renn Square rehearsal ring · ninety-four minutes before opening*

They returned to find the audience gates already crowded. Rumour had travelled faster than the festival notices: the youth troupe had refused the lattice, and the woman from the sky intended to abolish safety.

Illuminara asked the technicians to leave the lattice powered but remove its authority. Original speech would sound first. The display would show named human glosses side by side, with uncertainty visible instead of silently resolved.
Siva did not surrender the stop key.

**Siva**  
Any survivor or speaker can call a pause. Ninety seconds. No argument during the first thirty.

**Mara**  
And the person whose words are disputed speaks first after the pause.

**Lio**  
Not the loudest translator.

**Siva**  
Not the director.

Lio painted three amber circles on the stage floor. One for the speaker, one for the person harmed or alarmed, one for a chosen glosser. Nobody would be forced into a circle; an empty place would remain visible.

Illuminara stepped to the microphone with a list of twelve district and clan names. She could have analysed every mouth in the square and reproduced the sounds mechanically. Instead she used only what each person had freely taught her.

**Illuminara**  
I will say these as I currently hear them. If I am wrong, correct me. The correction will not be an interruption. It will be the work.
The first four names passed with small adjustments. On the fifth, she placed the stress too early. Laughter moved through the North-bank seats.
Illuminara heard delight before she understood the joke. It was bright, shared and entirely unavailable to flawless Standard.

**Lio**  
You just called the Lantern Boat clan the clan of damp trousers.

**Illuminara**  
How fortunate that I wore neither.
The laughter widened, including two people in survivor sashes. Siva did not laugh, but her hand eased around the key.
Then Illuminara reached Sena Marru-kei.
She spoke the first part correctly and let the final syllable fall. A man near the eastern gate stood so abruptly that his chair overturned.

**Man in the east seats**  
That ending is what they called us before the fires.
Several young performers answered at once. Their voices collided. The lattice flashed SAFE STANDARD AVAILABLE.
Siva struck the brass key.
Amber light filled the square. The microphones muted for thirty seconds, including Illuminara’s. She did not override them.

A barrier at the eastern aisle buckled as frightened people pressed backward. Illuminara crossed the distance in a blur, braced the rail with both hands and opened a second path without lifting anyone or deciding where they should go.
Mara reached the overturned chair. She righted it and faced the man.

**Mara**  
Do you want the middle circle, or do you want me to carry your words there?

**Man in the east seats**  
Carry them. I do not want all those eyes.
When the first thirty seconds ended, Mara entered the circle alone and repeated his objection. Lio waited in the speaker’s circle until she finished.

**Lio**  
My grandmother’s clan-name is Marru-kei. The insult uses the same last sound, but it cuts the first vowel short. I should have told the stage team before asking everyone to know the difference.

**Mara**  
Can the difference be shown before it is heard?

**Lio**  
A blue river mark. Our speakers already use it in letters.
Siva turned to the man. He remained beside his seat.

**Siva**  
Would the mark and the speaker-first rule be enough for rehearsal to continue?

**Man in the east seats**  
For rehearsal. Not a promise about tomorrow.

**Siva**  
That is all I asked.
The man studied the black survivor’s sash at Siva’s shoulder.

**Man in the east seats**  
I wore east-bank grey at the funerals after yours. We learned whose black sash kept the key. What was your brother’s name?

**Siva**  
Jaro.
He repeated it once in Standard. Siva corrected the rising vowel and the inward fold, not gently but exactly. He listened, then shook his head when Mara offered him a phrase card.

**Man in the east seats**  
Not yet.
The answer was not forgiveness. It was consent for the next bounded step.
Siva released the key. The blue river mark appeared beside Marru-kei, but the lattice also displayed the eastern listener’s warning and the two different vowel lengths.

**Illuminara**  
Sena Marru-kei.
This time Lio’s grandmother called from the front row.

**Sena**  
Closer. You still return the boat with only one fish.
The square laughed again, and the man in the east seats sat down instead of leaving.

scenes.title: The Ninety-Second Proof
paragraphs: *Renn Square · forty-eight minutes before opening*

Siva wrote the proof conditions on the main display herself. The rehearsal would use three phrases selected by survivors, three selected by performers and one selected without warning by a mixed audience panel. Any participant could call the ninety-second pause. The speaker could correct every display, and the correction would remain in the public record beside the earlier error.

**Siva**  
A machine failure does not void the proof if we catch it, honour the pause and keep the correction beside the error. One uncaught or concealed substitution, and we use Standard tonight.

**Lio**  
One ignored pause and we walk.

**Mara**  
One person mocked for correcting us and I close the survivor section.

**Illuminara**  
And if all seven phrases are repaired without threat or concealment?
Siva looked toward the archive stairs.

**Siva**  
Then I sign a licence for one night. Nothing more.
The first two phrases passed with both glosses visible, one South-bank blessing drawing startled laughter.
The third phrase used a kinship form Standard translated as dependent. Sena corrected it to the person whose bowl remains at my table even when absent.
At the fifth phrase, the lattice failed its two-second threshold. The screen displayed a confident translation while the human glossers were still divided.
Siva’s hand moved toward the stop key before anyone else called the pause.

**Siva**  
Hold.
She looked at the confident line still shining above Mara’s divided glossers. For one breath the square was twelve years younger: one frightened rendering wearing the authority of fact.

**Siva**  
The lattice has failed. The proof now is whether we catch the failure without hiding it or punishing the answer.
Amber light returned. This time no one surged. People put down their programmes and waited through the first silent thirty seconds.
The disputed phrase came from Mara. In her district it meant I remember what was taken. In Lio’s it sounded like I reserve the right to take it back.

**Mara**  
Both meanings live in it. I chose the first. I cannot make the second unreal.

**Lio**  
Then my gloss should say what I feared, not what you secretly meant.

**Mara**  
Yes. And mine should say what I intended, not what you were required to hear.
The two sentences appeared side by side. The lattice marked neither as final.
Siva stared at them. Twelve years earlier, the city had hidden precisely this kind of disagreement in order to prevent panic.

**Siva**  
What stops a liar from using uncertainty as a shield?

**Illuminara**  
Nothing automatic. The original recording remains. The affected person’s account remains. Consequences remain. Uncertainty prevents the translator from becoming a witness it was not.

**Mara**  
And the pause gives us time to ask who benefits from the ambiguity.

**Lio**  
A safeguard is not innocence.

Siva let the sentence sit. Then she added a rule: deliberate misuse would be reviewed by a rotating panel that could suspend a performer, but never erase the original speech or the objections attached to it.

Before the seventh phrase, the mixed panel offered the eastern man the blank card again. He could have passed it to anyone. After watching Mara’s correction remain beside the machine’s error, he wrote one word and folded the card shut.
The seventh phrase arrived unannounced to Siva from the eastern man. It was Jaro’s name in her home dialect.
The square became utterly still.
The lattice offered the Standard form. Lio’s glosser panel left the line blank and turned toward Siva.

**Lio**  
Speaker first.
Siva did not move for several breaths. No rule required her to speak. The empty amber circle remained open.
Then she stepped into it.

**Siva**  
His name rose here.
She touched her throat.

**Siva**  
And folded here, as if the sound were making room for the person who answered.
She said Jaro’s name. Lio repeated it and missed the fold.

**Siva**  
No. Not a door closing.

**Lio**  
Again, please.
She said it again. He listened again. On the third attempt, the shape held.
The eastern man called no pause. Mara did not ask Siva to forgive the city or the crowd. Sena simply moved a survivor’s chair closer to the stage.
Siva signed the one-night licence.

**Siva**  
Keep the lattice awake. Let it show how often it does not know.

scenes.title: A Boat Returned with Fish
paragraphs: *Renn Square · midnight*
The Festival of Returning Voices opened forty-one minutes late.

Every performance took longer than the programme allowed. Original speech came first. Two or three human glosses followed when they differed. Pale bars showed uncertainty. Blue river marks warned where a cherished name touched an old insult. Amber circles remained empty until someone freely entered them.
The youth troupe began with a comedy in three dialects about a ferryman who accepted payment in prophecies but could not make change.
Half the audience laughed before the first gloss. The other half laughed when the second gloss revealed that change also meant a dry pair of trousers.

Illuminara stood behind the eastern aisle, not on the stage. She repaired a cracked rail, carried water to a woman whose hands shook after a pause and listened as twelve districts corrected her festival greeting.
Three survivors chose to leave before the comedy. Their empty chairs were not removed or filled. Mara attached small cards to them: LEFT BY CHOICE. RETURN WELCOME. NO EXPLANATION OWED.

One performer was suspended after repeating an ambiguity for a cheap laugh when he had been warned it named a massacre. His original words, the objection and the panel’s decision remained visible in the record.
The festival did not prove that every living voice was safe. It proved that safety no longer required pretending only one voice was real.
Near midnight, Lio rolled out the restored opening banner. The twelfth line read SENA MARRU-KEI, with the blue river mark and a note inviting the bearer’s own account.
Sena examined it sternly.

**Sena**  
The fish is too small.

**Lio**  
It is a symbol, Grandmother.

**Sena**  
Then symbolise generosity.
He painted a larger fish. The audience applauded the correction, not the painter.

Siva watched from the safety console. The green field that once counted years without reported language incidents now showed tonight’s totals: eleven pauses, eleven resumptions, twenty-eight public corrections, no hidden substitutions and no assaults.

**Mara**  
Will you keep it?

**Siva**  
The one-night licence expires at dawn.
Mara waited.

**Siva**  
At dawn I will propose thirty nights. Rotating panels. Survivor veto over the pause rules, not over other people’s names. Speaker ownership of corrections. Independent audit of every confident machine gloss.
Mara unfolded one of the spare chairs and placed it beside the console rather than behind it.

**Mara**  
If the survivor section chooses me, I take the first dawn rotation.

**Siva**  
You said you would not choose between two dangers.

**Mara**  
I will not. I can help hold the pause without becoming its only keeper. So can you.
Siva looked from Mara’s chair to the eleven recorded resumptions. The brass key no longer sat beneath one hand.

**Illuminara**  
I cannot promise to be here when the next joke turns dangerous.

**Siva**  
No. But the record will be, and Mara will not be alone at this console. Leave us something we can practise without you.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will leave the listening equipment, and you will keep the right to change the practice.

**Mara**  
And if the council refuses?

**Siva**  
Then I will show them tonight’s record and ask them which risk they are pretending does not exist.
She removed the black survivor’s sash, folded it carefully and placed it beside the brass stop key. She did not discard either.
Lio approached with a wet brush and enough restraint not to threaten her coat.

**Lio**  
There is space on the banner for Jaro, if you want it.

**Siva**  
Not as a reason everyone must agree with me.

**Lio**  
As a person whose name should not be made square.
Siva took the brush. She painted the rising mark first, then the inward fold. Her hand shook on the final stroke, and nobody reached over to steady it without being asked.
When she stepped back, Illuminara said the name once.
Siva listened.

**Siva**  
Closer.

**Illuminara**  
Only closer?

**Siva**  
Closer is how a living language says continue.
Above them, the twelve ribbons pulled differently in the river wind. Their knots held because none had been forced to become the same ribbon.

critic_line: In a city where a flawless translation system once let one frightened rendering pass for fact, Illuminara listens to a recording until she hears a flood warning under the word the transcript called a threat, then helps Siva and the festival replace the machine's final word with a public pause, side-by-side glosses and speaker-owned corrections, so a banner name is restored and nobody is forced to forgive.

shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-heavy, with a strong central idea: translation that flattens meaning, and a repair practice. The Jaro name-correction scene and Sena's fish jokes carry real warmth. Weaknesses are procedural rule-listing in the middle, a tidy resolution, and many names to track, which may slow some readers.

A humane, dialogue-rich conflict turns translation ethics into vivid public action, with memorable names, pauses, and corrections. The emotional repair feels earned, especially through Siva, though the procedural demonstrations and repeated thesis statements make the latter half somewhat didactic and overextended.

translation_sl.title: FESTIVAL NAPAČNO IZGOVORJENIH IMEN
translation_sl.deck: Popoln prevajalski sistem je v mestu ohranjal mir tako, da je zgladil vsako nevarno besedo. V noči, ko ljudje končno nočejo več govoriti skozenj, jim mora Illuminara pomagati tvegati, da bodo slišani, ne da bi stare rane razglasila za nepomembne.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov. Mestna otvoritev se sesuje, ko varnostna mreža izbriše živo rodovno ime; arhiv razkrije, da je stari izgred utrdil en sam prevod, ki mu ni bilo mogoče ugovarjati; iskrena javna napačna izgovorjava postane popravilo namesto iskre; časovno omejena vaja preizkusi varovala skupnosti pod pritiskom; festival pa se znova odpre s počasnejšim govorom, vidno negotovostjo, prostovoljno pravico do premora in povrnjenimi imeni.

scenes.title: Prazno mesto na praporu
paragraphs: *Trg Renn · tri ure pred otvoritveno povorko*

Dvanajst trakov je prečkalo trg od strehe do strehe, vsak stkan v drugačnem okrožnem vzorcu. Pod njimi je prevajalska mreža visela kot druga, nevidna streha: mikrofoni v napuščih, svetlobne črke ob odru in miren sintetični glas, pripravljen, da vsak stavek spremeni v brezhibni standardni jezik.

Na največjem praporu so bila imena mladih nastopajočih, ki naj bi odprli Festival vračajočih se glasov, ter Sena Marru-kei, spoštovane starešine, katere otvoritveni klic naj bi jim odgovoril. Enajst imen je sijalo v zlatu. V dvanajsti vrstici je pisalo SENA — NEPODPRT ELEMENT IMENA.
Lio Marr je stal na lestvi z lončkom rečno modre barve. Manjkajoče rodovno ime svoje babice je trikrat prebarval čez opozorilo. Vsakič ga je vzdrževalna luč mreže izbrisala.

**Lio**  
Če jo izbriše še enkrat, bom njeno ime naslikal čez direktorjev plašč.
Siva Renn ni dvignila pogleda z varnostne konzole. Nosila je črn trak preživelih iz časov starega jezika in en palec držala na medeninasti tipki za zaustavitev.

**Siva**  
Potem bo plašč odstranjen iz programa kot nepreverjena površina.

**Lio**  
To je bila skoraj šala.

**Siva**  
To je bilo opozorilo z dobrim občutkom za pravi trenutek.

Illuminara je pristala zunaj kroga luči za vaje, tako nežno, da se ni premaknil nobeden od papirnatih čolničkov okoli vodnjaka. Prišla je pomagati festivalu, da se začne, ne da bi obnovil nasilje, zaradi katerega so trg pred dvanajstimi leti zaprli.
Prebrala je prapor, nato pa pogledala Lia, ne stroja.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi moralo pisati v tej vrstici?
Lio je stopil z lestve. Praznega traku se je dotaknil z dvema prstoma, umazanima od barve.

**Lio**  
Sena Marru-kei. Marru-kei ni okras. Pomeni, da pripada ljudem, ki izposojeni čoln vrnejo z ribami. To je tudi zvok, s katerim jo je mati klicala domov.

**Siva**  
Ima štirinajst spornih razlag in eno opolzko podobnost v govoru južnega brega.

**Lio**  
Moja babica je stara enainosemdeset let. Ni sporna razlaga.
Ob vznožju odra je Mara Venn zložila stol za preživele in ga odnesla. Čez čeljust ji je tekla bela brazgotina, kjer se je med izgredom razbila steklenica.

**Mara**  
Tudi moja sestra ni bila. Beseda, ki v enih ustih zveni nedolžno, lahko iz drugih pride oborožena.
Trg okoli nje je utihnil. Lio je odložil čopič.

**Illuminara**  
Odhajate zato, ker je njegovo ime nevarno, ali zato, ker ga je mreža odstranila?

**Mara**  
Odhajam zato, ker so se vsi tukaj odločili, da moram izbirati med tema dvema nevarnostma.
Siva je končno dvignila pogled. Konzola je kazala polje zelenih potrditev: dvanajst let brez napada v mestnem območju, ki bi ga sprožil jezik.

**Siva**  
Mreža vsakomur da isti varni stavek. Nikomur ni treba ugibati, kaj je bilo mišljeno.

**Lio**  
Nihče pa ne more misliti ničesar, česar stroj ne more sploščiti.
Za njim so člani mladinske skupine drug za drugim sneli grlene mikrofone. Zavrnitev ni spremljal noben napev. Dovolj so bili drobni kliki kovine ob les.

**Siva**  
Če govorite brez posredovanja, otvoritveno dovoljenje ne velja.

**Lio**  
Potem otvoritve ne bo.

Illuminara je opazovala, kako se Sivina roka zateguje okoli tipke za zaustavitev. To ni bila cenzorka, ki bi uživala v poslušnosti. Bila je oseba, ki je držala vrata zaprta, ker je nekoč videla, kako je skoznje prišla množica z ognjem.

**Illuminara**  
Pokažite mi stavek, zaradi katerega ste to zgradili.
Sivin obraz se je zaprl.

**Siva**  
Ni bilo stavka. Bil je pogreb.

**Illuminara**  
Potem mi natančno pokažite pogreb.
Mara se je ustavila ob praznih stolih. Po dolgem trenutku je enega postavila nazaj.

**Mara**  
Zaradi tega bom ostala. Ne zaradi lekcije. Zaradi natančnosti.

scenes.title: Prevod, ki mu ni bilo mogoče odgovoriti
paragraphs: *Mestni arhiv pod Trgom Renn · dve uri in sedemnajst minut pred otvoritvijo*

Arhiv je izgred hranil v treh sobah, ki se med seboj niso strinjale. V eni so bili poškodovani posnetki. V drugi uradni prepisi. V zadnji predmeti, ki so jih ljudje odnesli domov: ožgan boben, rdeč otroški čevelj, napis, razklan skozi besedo REKA.
Siva je odklenila sobo s posnetki, vendar je ostala v vratih.

**Siva**  
Moj brat Jaro je imel devetnajst let. Slišal je bobnarja s severnega brega izreči izziv. Odgovoril mu je. Do sončnega zahoda je bilo mrtvih sedem ljudi.

**Lio**  
To je šolska različica.

**Siva**  
To je tudi različica, v kateri sem z rokavov spirala njegovo kri.
Lio je pogledal navzdol. Njegova jeza ni izginila, izgubila pa je preprosto obliko, ki jo je nosila na trgu.

**Lio**  
Žal mi je zaradi Jara.

**Siva**  
Ne uporabljaj ga kot ceno svojega poguma.
Illuminara je prosila za izvirni posnetek, ne za potrjeni prepis. Arhivist ga je označil kot nerazumljivega, ker so se trije govorci prekrivali, ritem bobna pa je prekinjal soglasnike.
Enkrat ga je poslušala pri človeški hitrosti. Nato ga je poslušala znova, ločila zračne vibracije, ne da bi jih spremenila, in pustila, da je vsak glas zazvenel skozi drugo stensko ploščo.
Ženski glas je izrekel besedno zvezo v govoru severnega brega. Uradni prepis jo je prevedel kot VZEMITE JIM REČNI BREG PRED MRAKOM.
Boben pod besedno zvezo je uporabljal ritem opozorila pred poplavo, ne ritma izziva.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj še lahko pomeni glagol?

**Lio**  
Držati. Ohraniti. Opirati z lastnim telesom.

**Mara**  
Ali ne popustiti.

**Siva**  
V Jarovem okrožju pa nekomu vzeti.

Illuminara je prešla na naslednji posnetek. Starešina s severnega brega je štirinajst sekund po prvem prevodu poskušala prekiniti mestni prenos. Njen mikrofon so zaprli, ker je uradni kanal dovoljeval eno samo potrjeno razlago.
Po enaintridesetih sekundah je drug prevajalec poslal DRŽITE POPLAVNI NASIP SKUPAJ. Prenos je prevod označil kot protisloven in ga potlačil.
Po oseminštiridesetih sekundah se je razbila prva steklenica.
Siva je zaporedje predvajala še enkrat. Nato še enkrat. Ob tretjem predvajanju je sedla poleg ožganega bobna.

**Siva**  
Pravite, da je bil izgred programska napaka.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Ljudje so metali steklenice, izbirali tarče in ubijali. Napaka ni odpravila njihove odgovornosti. Toda mesto je enemu prestrašenemu prevodu dalo veljavo dejstva in vsakemu živemu govorcu odreklo pravico, da mu odgovori.

**Mara**  
Rekli so nam, da bo gotovost zadržala paniko.

**Lio**  
Gotovost je zaklenila napačna vrata.
Siva se je dotaknila razklanega napisa in s konico prsta sledila ožganemu robu.

**Siva**  
Dvanajst let tukaj ni nihče umrl zaradi besede.

**Illuminara**  
Dvanajst let nihče ni smel ugotoviti, ali lahko besedo popravi.
Siva je vstala tako hitro, da je stol udaril ob steno.

**Siva**  
Po aplavzu boste odšli. Jaz bom tukaj, ko bo šala znova postala pogreb.
Besede so pristale brez gledališke sile. Imele so natančno težo, ki jo je ves čas nosila.
Illuminara ni takoj odgovorila. Pogledala je Jarovo ime v uradnem prepisu. Zadnji samoglasnik so poenotili v standardni jezik.

**Illuminara**  
Kako je izgovarjal svoje ime?

**Siva**  
To ni pomembno za napako nadzora.

**Illuminara**  
Pomembno je za vas.
Sivin prvi poskus je bil komaj slišen. Ime se je na koncu dvignilo, nato pa se je ob zadnjem dihu zavihalo navznoter. Prepis ga je naredil odrezavega in oglatega.
Illuminara je ponovila, kar je slišala, in zgrešila zavih.

**Siva**  
Ne. Zaradi vas zveni, kakor da se zapirajo vrata.

**Illuminara**  
Še enkrat, prosim.
Siva ga je izgovorila še enkrat. Illuminara je znova poslušala. Tretji poskus je bil še vedno nepopoln, vendar je Siva ni ustavila.

**Mara**  
Kaj se je spremenilo?

**Illuminara**  
Mislila sem, da potrebujemo prevajalski sistem, ki naredi manj napak. Potrebujemo javno prakso, ki prepreči, da bi katerakoli napaka postala taka, da ji ni mogoče odgovoriti.

**Siva**  
Praksa ni pregrada.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne zaupajte zamisli. Zasnujte preizkus, dovolj strog, da bi lahko zaupali rezultatu.

scenes.title: Izgovori narobe tam, kjer lahko slišimo
paragraphs: *Krog za vaje na Trgu Renn · štiriindevetdeset minut pred otvoritvijo*

Ko so se vrnili, so bila vrata za občinstvo že oblegana. Govorice so potovale hitreje od festivalskih obvestil: mladinska skupina je zavrnila mrežo, ženska z neba pa naj bi nameravala odpraviti varnost.

Illuminara je tehnike prosila, naj mrežo pustijo vključeno, vendar ji odvzamejo avtoriteto. Najprej naj bi zazvenel izvirni govor. Zaslon naj bi vzporedno kazal poimensko navedene človeške razlage, negotovost pa naj bi bila vidna namesto tiho razrešena.
Siva ni izpustila tipke za zaustavitev.

**Siva**  
Vsak preživeli ali govorec lahko zahteva premor. Devetdeset sekund. Prvih trideset brez prerekanja.

**Mara**  
Oseba, katere besede so sporne, po premoru govori prva.

**Lio**  
Ne najglasnejši prevajalec.

**Siva**  
Ne direktor.

Lio je na tla odra naslikal tri jantarne kroge. Enega za govorca, enega za prizadeto ali prestrašeno osebo, enega za izbranega razlagalca. Nihče ne bi bil prisiljen stopiti v krog; prazno mesto bi ostalo vidno.

Illuminara je stopila k mikrofonu s seznamom dvanajstih okrožnih in rodovnih imen. Lahko bi analizirala vsaka usta na trgu in mehansko poustvarila glasove. Namesto tega je uporabila le tisto, česar jo je vsak človek prostovoljno naučil.

**Illuminara**  
Izgovorila jih bom tako, kot jih trenutno slišim. Če se motim, me popravite. Popravek ne bo prekinitev. To bo delo.
Prva štiri imena so šla skozi z majhnimi prilagoditvami. Pri petem je naglas postavila prezgodaj. Skozi sedeže severnega brega se je razlegel smeh.
Illuminara je zaslišala veselje, še preden je razumela šalo. Bilo je svetlo, skupno in brezhibnemu standardnemu jeziku povsem nedostopno.

**Lio**  
Pravkar ste rod Svetilniškega čolna imenovali rod vlažnih hlač.

**Illuminara**  
Kakšna sreča, da ne nosim ne enega ne drugega.
Smeh se je razširil in zajel dva človeka s trakovi preživelih. Siva se ni smejala, vendar je njen prijem okoli tipke popustil.
Nato je Illuminara prišla do Sena Marru-kei.
Prvi del je izgovorila pravilno, zadnji zlog pa pustila pasti. Moški blizu vzhodnih vrat je vstal tako sunkovito, da je prevrnil stol.

**Moški na vzhodnih sedežih**  
S takšno končnico so nas klicali pred požari.
Več mladih nastopajočih je odgovorilo hkrati. Njihovi glasovi so trčili. Mreža je utripnila VAREN STANDARDNI JEZIK NA VOLJO.
Siva je udarila po medeninasti tipki.
Jantarna svetloba je napolnila trg. Mikrofoni so za trideset sekund utihnili, tudi Illuminara je ostala brez svojega. Ni jih preglasila.

Pregrada ob vzhodnem prehodu se je uklonila, ko so se prestrašeni ljudje stisnili nazaj. Illuminara je v hipu premagala razdaljo, z obema rokama podprla ograjo in odprla drugo pot, ne da bi kogarkoli dvignila ali odločila, kam naj gre.
Mara je prišla do prevrnjenega stola. Postavila ga je pokonci in se obrnila k moškemu.

**Mara**  
Želite v srednji krog ali naj tja odnesem vaše besede?

**Moški na vzhodnih sedežih**  
Odnesite jih. Nočem vseh teh pogledov.
Ko se je prvih trideset sekund končalo, je Mara sama stopila v krog in ponovila njegov ugovor. Lio je čakal v govorčevem krogu, dokler ni končala.

**Lio**  
Rodovno ime moje babice je Marru-kei. Žaljivka ima enak zadnji glas, vendar je njen prvi samoglasnik krajši. To bi moral povedati odrski ekipi, preden sem od vseh pričakoval, da poznajo razliko.

**Mara**  
Ali je mogoče razliko pokazati, preden jo slišimo?

**Lio**  
Z modrim rečnim znamenjem. Naši govorci ga že uporabljajo v pisavi.
Siva se je obrnila k moškemu. Ostal je ob svojem sedežu.

**Siva**  
Bi bila znamenje in pravilo, da govori najprej govorec, dovolj za nadaljevanje vaje?

**Moški na vzhodnih sedežih**  
Za vajo. Ne kot obljuba za jutri.

**Siva**  
Samo to sem vprašala.
Moški si je ogledal črni trak preživelih na Sivini rami.

**Moški na vzhodnih sedežih**  
Na pogrebih po vaših sem nosil sivino vzhodnega brega. Izvedeli smo, kdo je bila preživela v črnem traku, ki je držala tipko. Kako je bilo ime vašemu bratu?

**Siva**  
Jaro.
Enkrat ga je ponovil v standardnem jeziku. Siva je popravila dvig samoglasnika in zavih navznoter, ne nežno, temveč natančno. Poslušal je, nato pa odkimal, ko mu je Mara ponudila kartico z zapisom.

**Moški na vzhodnih sedežih**  
Ne še.
Odgovor ni bil odpuščanje. Bil je soglasje za naslednji omejeni korak.
Siva je spustila tipko. Modro rečno znamenje se je pojavilo ob Marru-kei, vendar je mreža prikazala tudi opozorilo vzhodnega poslušalca in različni dolžini samoglasnika.

**Illuminara**  
Sena Marru-kei.
Tokrat jo je Liova babica poklicala iz prve vrste.

**Sena**  
Bliže. Še vedno vračate čoln z eno samo ribo.
Trg se je znova zasmejal, moški na vzhodnih sedežih pa je sedel, namesto da bi odšel.

scenes.title: Devetdesetsekundni dokaz
paragraphs: *Trg Renn · oseminštirideset minut pred otvoritvijo*

Siva je sama napisala pogoje dokaza na glavni zaslon. Pri vaji bi uporabili tri besedne zveze, ki bi jih izbrali preživeli, tri, ki bi jih izbrali nastopajoči, in eno, ki bi jo brez opozorila izbrala mešana skupina občinstva. Vsak udeleženec bi lahko zahteval devetdesetsekundni premor. Govorec bi lahko popravil vsak prikaz, popravek pa bi ostal v javnem zapisu poleg prejšnje napake.

**Siva**  
Napaka stroja ne razveljavi dokaza, če jo ujamemo, spoštujemo premor in ohranimo popravek ob napaki. Ena sama neodkrita ali prikrita zamenjava in nocoj uporabimo standardni jezik.

**Lio**  
En sam prezrt premor in odidemo.

**Mara**  
En človek, ki se mu posmehujejo, ker nas je popravil, in zaprem oddelek za preživele.

**Illuminara**  
In če vseh sedem besednih zvez popravimo brez grožnje ali prikrivanja?
Siva je pogledala proti arhivskim stopnicam.

**Siva**  
Potem podpišem dovoljenje za eno noč. Nič več.
Prvi dve besedni zvezi sta šli skozi z obema vidnima razlagama, en blagoslov južnega brega pa je sprožil presenečen smeh.
Tretja besedna zveza je uporabila sorodstveno obliko, ki jo je standardni jezik prevedel kot vzdrževanec. Sena jo je popravila v oseba, katere skleda ostane na moji mizi tudi takrat, ko je ni.
Pri peti besedni zvezi je mreža zgrešila svoj dvosekundni prag. Zaslon je prikazal samozavesten prevod, medtem ko so se človeški razlagalci še vedno razhajali.
Sivina roka se je premaknila proti tipki za zaustavitev, še preden je kdorkoli drug zahteval premor.

**Siva**  
Premor.
Pogledala je samozavestno vrstico, ki je še vedno sijala nad Marinimi razdeljenimi razlagalci. Za en dih je bil trg dvanajst let mlajši: en prestrašen prevod je nosil veljavo dejstva.

**Siva**  
Mreža je odpovedala. Dokaz je zdaj v tem, ali bomo napako ujeli, ne da bi jo skrili ali kaznovali odgovor.
Jantarna svetloba se je vrnila. Tokrat ni nihče planil. Ljudje so odložili programe in počakali skozi prvih trideset tihih sekund.
Sporna besedna zveza je prišla od Mare. V njenem okrožju je pomenila spominjam se, kaj je bilo odvzeto. V Liovem je zvenela kot pridržujem si pravico, da to vzamem nazaj.

**Mara**  
Oba pomena živita v njej. Izbrala sem prvega. Drugega ne morem narediti neresničnega.

**Lio**  
Potem naj moja razlaga pove, česa sem se bal, ne tega, kar naj bi ti na skrivaj mislila.

**Mara**  
Da. In moja naj pove, kaj sem nameravala, ne tega, kar si moral slišati.
Stavka sta se pojavila drug ob drugem. Mreža nobenega ni označila kot dokončnega.
Siva je strmela vanju. Pred dvanajstimi leti je mesto skrilo prav takšno nesoglasje, da bi preprečilo paniko.

**Siva**  
Kaj lažnivcu prepreči, da bi negotovost uporabil kot ščit?

**Illuminara**  
Nič samodejnega. Izvirni posnetek ostane. Pripoved prizadete osebe ostane. Posledice ostanejo. Negotovost prepreči prevajalcu, da bi postal priča nečemu, čemur ni bil priča.

**Mara**  
Premor pa nam da čas, da vprašamo, komu dvoumnost koristi.

**Lio**  
Varovalo ni nedolžnost.

Siva je pustila, da je stavek obležal. Nato je dodala pravilo: namerno zlorabo bi pregledal izmenjujoči se odbor, ki bi lahko nastopajočega izključil, vendar nikoli ne bi izbrisal izvirnega govora ali ugovorov, pripetih nanj.

Pred sedmo besedno zvezo je mešana skupina vzhodnemu moškemu znova ponudila prazno kartico. Lahko bi jo predal komurkoli. Ko je opazoval, kako je Marin popravek ostal ob napaki stroja, je napisal eno besedo in kartico prepognil.
Sedma besedna zveza je k Sivi prišla brez opozorila od vzhodnega moškega. Bilo je Jarovo ime v njenem domačem narečju.
Trg je popolnoma utihnil.
Mreža je ponudila standardno obliko. Liova skupina razlagalcev je pustila vrstico prazno in se obrnila k Sivi.

**Lio**  
Najprej govorec.
Siva se več vdihov ni premaknila. Nobeno pravilo ni zahtevalo, da govori. Prazen jantarni krog je ostal odprt.
Nato je stopila vanj.

**Siva**  
Njegovo ime se je dvignilo tukaj.
Dotaknila se je grla.

**Siva**  
In se zavihalo tukaj, kakor da zvok dela prostor za človeka, ki je odgovoril.
Izgovorila je Jarovo ime. Lio ga je ponovil in zgrešil zavih.

**Siva**  
Ne. Ne kot vrata, ki se zapirajo.

**Lio**  
Še enkrat, prosim.
Izgovorila ga je še enkrat. On je znova poslušal. V tretjem poskusu je oblika vzdržala.
Vzhodni moški ni zahteval premora. Mara ni prosila Sive, naj odpusti mestu ali množici. Sena je preprosto premaknila stol za preživele bliže odru.
Siva je podpisala dovoljenje za eno noč.

**Siva**  
Mreža naj ostane budna. Naj pokaže, kako pogosto ne ve.

scenes.title: Čoln, vrnjen z ribami
paragraphs: *Trg Renn · polnoč*
Festival vračajočih se glasov se je začel enainštirideset minut pozno.

Vsak nastop je trajal dlje, kot je dovoljeval program. Najprej je zazvenel izvirni govor. Ko so se razlikovale, so sledile dve ali tri človeške razlage. Blede črte so kazale negotovost. Modra rečna znamenja so opozarjala, kje se je dragoceno ime dotikalo stare žaljivke. Jantarni krogi so ostali prazni, dokler ni kdo prostovoljno stopil vanje.
Mladinska skupina je začela s komedijo v treh narečjih o brodarju, ki je sprejemal plačilo v prerokbah, ni pa znal vrniti drobiža.
Pol občinstva se je zasmejalo pred prvo razlago. Druga polovica se je zasmejala, ko je druga razlaga razkrila, da sprememba pomeni tudi suhe hlače.

Illuminara je stala za vzhodnim prehodom, ne na odru. Popravila je razpokano ograjo, odnesla vodo ženski, ki so se ji po premoru tresle roke, in poslušala, ko je dvanajst okrožij popravljalo njen festivalski pozdrav.

Trije preživeli so se odločili oditi pred komedijo. Njihovih praznih stolov niso odstranili ali zapolnili. Mara je nanje pritrdila majhne kartice: ODŠEL PO LASTNI IZBIRI. VRNITEV DOBRODOŠLA. POJASNILO NI POTREBNO.
Enega nastopajočega so izključili, ker je za poceni smeh ponovil dvoumnost, potem ko so ga opozorili, da poimenuje pokol. Njegove izvirne besede, ugovor in odločitev odbora so ostali vidni v zapisu.
Festival ni dokazal, da je vsak živ glas varen. Dokazal je, da varnost ne zahteva več pretvarjanja, da je resničen samo en glas.
Blizu polnoči je Lio razvil obnovljeni otvoritveni prapor. V dvanajsti vrstici je pisalo SENA MARRU-KEI z modrim rečnim znamenjem in opombo, ki je vabila k lastni pripovedi nosilke imena.
Sena ga je strogo preučila.

**Sena**  
Riba je premajhna.

**Lio**  
Simbol je, babica.

**Sena**  
Potem simboliziraj radodarnost.
Naslikal je večjo ribo. Občinstvo je zaploskalo popravku, ne slikarju.

Siva je opazovala z varnostne konzole. Zeleno polje, ki je nekoč štelo leta brez prijavljenih jezikovnih incidentov, je zdaj kazalo nocojšnje seštevke: enajst premorov, enajst nadaljevanj, osemindvajset javnih popravkov, nobene prikrite zamenjave in nobenega napada.

**Mara**  
Ga boste obdržali?

**Siva**  
Dovoljenje za eno noč poteče ob zori.
Mara je počakala.

**Siva**  
Ob zori bom predlagala trideset noči. Izmenjujoče se odbore. Veto preživelih nad pravili za premor, ne nad imeni drugih ljudi. Lastništvo govorcev nad popravki. Neodvisno revizijo vsake samozavestne strojne razlage.
Mara je razgrnila enega od rezervnih stolov in ga postavila ob konzolo, ne za njo.

**Mara**  
Če me izbere oddelek preživelih, prevzamem prvo izmeno ob zori.

**Siva**  
Rekli ste, da ne boste izbirali med dvema nevarnostma.

**Mara**  
Ne bom. Lahko pomagam držati premor, ne da bi postala njegova edina varuhinja. Tudi vi lahko.
Siva je pogledala z Marinega stola k enajstim zabeleženim nadaljevanjem. Medeninasta tipka ni več ležala pod eno samo roko.

**Illuminara**  
Ne morem obljubiti, da bom tukaj, ko bo naslednja šala postala nevarna.

**Siva**  
Ne. Toda zapis bo, Mara pa ne bo sama za to konzolo. Pustite nam nekaj, kar lahko vadimo brez vas.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom pustila opremo za poslušanje, vi pa boste obdržali pravico, da prakso spremenite.

**Mara**  
Kaj pa, če svet zavrne?

**Siva**  
Potem jim bom pokazala nocojšnji zapis in jih vprašala, katerega tveganja se pretvarjajo, da ni.
Snela je črni trak preživelih, ga skrbno zložila in položila ob medeninasto tipko za zaustavitev. Nobenega ni zavrgla.
Lio se je približal z mokrim čopičem in dovolj zadržanosti, da ni ogrožal njenega plašča.

**Lio**  
Na praporu je prostor za Jara, če ga želite.

**Siva**  
Ne kot razlog, da se morajo vsi strinjati z menoj.

**Lio**  
Kot človeka, čigar ime ne bi smelo postati oglato.
Siva je vzela čopič. Najprej je naslikala znamenje za dvig, nato zavih navznoter. Roka se ji je pri zadnji potezi zatresla, nihče pa se ni stegnil, da bi jo brez vprašanja umiril.
Ko je stopila nazaj, je Illuminara enkrat izgovorila ime.
Siva je poslušala.

**Siva**  
Bliže.

**Illuminara**  
Samo bliže?

**Siva**  
Bliže je način, kako živ jezik reče nadaljuj.
Nad njimi je rečni veter vlekel dvanajst trakov v različne smeri. Njihovi vozli so držali, ker noben trak ni bil prisiljen postati enak drugemu.

translation_sl.critic_line: V mestu, kjer je brezhiben prevajalski sistem nekoč dovolil, da je ena prestrašena razlaga obveljala za dejstvo, Illuminara posluša posnetek, dokler pod besedo, ki jo je prepis imenoval grožnja, ne zasliši opozorila pred poplavo; nato Sivi in festivalu pomaga zadnjo besedo stroja zamenjati z javnim premorom, vzporednimi razlagami in popravki, ki pripadajo govorcu, tako da se ime vrne na prapor in nikogar ni treba prisiliti k odpuščanju.
